title: How I use AI across my browser boxing game: boxer bios, fight recaps, and all the art
author: boxing-boxing
selftext:
Wanted to share some of the ways I'm using AI in my project, figured this is the right crowd for it.

I make a browser boxing game, and AI is baked into the whole thing at this point.

Boxer descriptions: I don't write them by hand. I feed the model the boxer's current appearance (gear, outfits, all that), their punch stats, and their fight record, and it writes the bio. A guy on a losing streak with brawler stats reads totally different from an undefeated technician. And it stays in sync as the boxer changes, new look or a few more KO wins and the description shifts with it.

Fight summaries: after every fight the game generates a written recap from the actual fight data, so the summary reflects what really happened instead of some generic template.

Artwork: all AI generated. Honestly it took a ton of iterations to get right, and it didn't start looking decent until Astra. Before that it was rough.

Example boxer profile: [https://browserboxing.com/boxers/webmaster](https://browserboxing.com/boxers/webmaster)

Curious how other people here are using generated text in their games, especially keeping the tone consistent across a ton of outputs. That's been the hardest part on my end.
